t: The Romans built two lines of fortifications round Alesia, an inner one against the besieged Gauls and an outer one against the relief force, and the Gauls' combined attacks on them failed.
Caesar's figure of a quarter of a million for the relief force is probably an exaggeration; modern historians usually think a number between 50,000 and 100,000 more credible.
Alesia was the last major engagement between Gauls and Romans and the end of generalised, organised resistance, although Gaul did not become a Roman province until 27 BCE.
dyk: Excavations at Alise-Sainte-Reine in the 1860s, funded by Napoleon III, uncovered evidence of Roman camps, and a statue of Vercingetorix was then dedicated at the site.
ev: Caesar becomes proconsul of Cisalpine Gaul, Illyricum and Gallia Narbonensis and begins the Gallic Wars
Caesar announces that Gaul is to be treated as a Roman province
Vercingetorix unites a coalition of Gauls and revolts, and the Romans take Avaricum
Caesar is defeated at Gergovia and then beats Vercingetorix's cavalry at the Vingeanne
Caesar besieges Alesia, fends off the relief force and receives Vercingetorix's surrender
Caesar crosses the Rubicon, beginning the Roman Civil War
Vercingetorix is paraded in Caesar's triumph and garrotted
Gallic territories north of Gallia Narbonensis become a Roman province under Augustus

f.place: Around the Gallic oppidum of Alesia, a centre of the Mandubii, most probably on Mont Auxois above Alise-Sainte-Reine in the Côte-d'Or, France
f.sides: Rome under the proconsul Julius Caesar, against a confederation of Gallic tribes under Vercingetorix of the Arverni; about 80,000 men are said to have been in Alesia, and the relief force is put at a quarter of a million by Caesar and at 50,000 to 100,000 by modern historians
f.outcome: The relief force was beaten off and fled, Vercingetorix surrendered, and the Gallic revolt collapsed
